slides.title: One tells you **what it can't do**
slides.sub: Guess which one we'd let near your customers.
slides.scene: At a market stall, a flashy salesman in a shiny suit holds up a gadget sparkling with fake glitter while Phoney the blue phone character stands at the next stall behind a plain, tidy box with a short handwritten-looking list pinned to it (abstract scribbles only); a shopper looks back and forth suspiciously between them.

left.label: ❌ The shiny one
left.text: Claims it does everything. Tested on real customers. Forgotten after launch.

right.label: ✅ The boring one
right.text: Lists what it doesn't do yet. Tested on made-up data first. Watched after launch.

slides.label: Before
slides.caption: Testing on real people is how you find out **in public**.
slides.scene: A cheerful cartoon robot carries a towering cake into a packed party, and the cake is visibly about to topple onto the guests; the guests duck in slow motion, one lifting a plate as a shield. Slapstick, bright, funny, no text.

slides.label: After
slides.caption: A **staging copy** with made-up data takes the fall instead.
slides.scene: Phoney the blue phone character calmly tests a wobbly cake in an empty rehearsal room full of cardboard cut-out guests; the cake falls over onto a cut-out, and Phoney the blue phone character shrugs, taking a note on a clipboard, entirely unbothered.

items.title: Your AI asks before anything that matters
Each app says what it cannot do

slides.text: A tool that claims to do everything is advertising, not a tool.
